subject: Clarify SIG Q6 (data classification) + Q12 (backup encryption scope) — FinBank
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood SIG — initial answers + two ambiguous items (Q6, Q12)

Hi Emily,

Thanks for sending the updated SIG template — we attached our completed draft (SIG_v2_answers.xlsx). Most items were pretty straightforward; two items came up as ambiguous when mapping to our hosted + private deployment model and I wanted to flag them so we can agree on a single interpretation:

- Q6 (Data classification): the question reads "Do you classify customer data and restrict processing based on classification levels?" — Redwood's control plane stores metadata, while customer data may be stored in customer VPCs (Private) or our hosted storage (Hosted). For hosted accounts we can apply tenant-level tags and separation; for Private deployments the customer controls classification.
- Q12 (Backups & encryption scope): It asks whether "backups of customer data are encrypted in transit and at rest, and who holds the KMS keys." We need to be explicit about our hosted default (Redwood-managed keys in KMS) vs. Private (customer KMS/HSM). Also need to state whether snapshots for autoscaling (ephemeral caching) are considered backups.

Rather than guess, would you prefer a short call to agree on the written interpretation we should put in the SIG answers, or should we provide both variants (hosted + private) in the spreadsheet? I'm happy to propose precise wording to paste into the SIG.

Attaching: SIG_v2_answers.xlsx (draft), redwood-network-diagram.pdf

Next steps suggested: either 30-min sync (I can host) or we send a tracked change version with both options and you mark which applies to FinBank.

Thanks —
Soojin

--

Subject: Re: Redwood SIG — initial answers + two ambiguous items (Q6, Q12)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks — we reviewed the draft. A short clarification before a call: for FinBank, Q6 means we expect product-level enforcement of classification (e.g., the vendor must be able to tag, filter, and prevent processing for "Restricted" datasets). If Redwood's Private deployment puts classification controls entirely in our environment that's OK, but for Hosted we'd need an explicit mechanism.

On Q12, our procurement team is strict: backups are within scope if they are restorable to production (i.e., not ephemeral caches). We need to know if Redwood's snapshots used for scale-up are considered customer-backups. Also want to confirm who controls keys for hosted accounts.

We agree a 30-min call is best — are you available Mon 5/25 10am PT or Tue 5/26 11:30am PT?

Best,
Emily

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-24T08:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SIG — initial answers + two ambiguous items (Q6, Q12)

Emily —

Mon 5/25 10am PT works for us. I'll send an invite.

To be productive on the call, here are two proposed, concise interpretations we can present:

- Proposed interpretation for Q6 (Data classification): "Vendor provides mechanisms to enable product-level data classification and enforcement for hosted customers (tenant-level tags, policy controls to prevent processing of restricted classes). For Private deployments, the customer maintains classification enforcement and configuration; vendor responsibilities are limited to providing tooling and documentation."

- Proposed interpretation for Q12 (Backups & encryption scope): "Backups are defined as persisted, restorable snapshots of customer data intended for recovery (not ephemeral cache copies used for scaling). For hosted accounts, backups are encrypted in transit and at rest by default; Redwood uses provider KMS with Redwood-managed keys unless a customer elects a customer-managed KMS for hosted+dedicated plans. For Private deployments, customers retain control of KMS/HSM."

I'll label these as Option A (hosted default) and Option B (private) in the spreadsheet. If FinBank needs Option A to include an explicit customer-managed KMS for hosted, we can note that as a procurement requirement in the SIG response.

Invite will include a short agenda: 1) confirm definitions (Q6, Q12), 2) agree wording to paste into SIG, 3) next steps for attestation.

See you Monday.

— Soojin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@finbank.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-25T10:50:00-07:00
Subject: Call notes and suggested SIG wording (summary)

Hi Emily / team —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick summary and the exact wording we propose to add to the SIG spreadsheet (we made tracked changes in the attached SIG_v2_answers.xlsx):

Meeting takeaways (short):
- FinBank requires product-level classification enforcement for hosted customers where the vendor processes customer data marked as "Restricted". Private deployments remain customer-controlled.
- Snapshots used purely for autoscaling cache are not considered backups; persisted snapshots intended for recovery/restore are backups and are in-scope.
- For hosted accounts, Redwood's default uses Redwood-managed provider KMS keys; if FinBank requires customer-managed keys for hosted we will mark that as an approval/upgrade path and include the procurement note.

Proposed SIG answers (exact text to paste):
Q6: "Redwood supports product-level data classification and enforcement for hosted accounts via tenant tags and policy controls that can prevent processing of data classified as 'Restricted'. For Private deployments, enforcement of classification is configured and controlled by the customer."

Q12: "Backups are defined as persisted, restorable snapshots of customer data intended for recovery. Snapshots created solely for ephemeral scaling or cache are not backups and are excluded. Backups in hosted accounts are encrypted in transit and at rest by default. By default Redwood uses provider KMS keys managed by Redwood; customers may elect customer-managed KMS/HSM for hosted or Private deployments as part of contract setup."

Action items:
- Emily: confirm whether FinBank wants hosted accounts to require customer-managed KMS by default (answer yes/no) — due 2026-05-27.
- Soojin: update SIG_v2_answers.xlsx with the agreed text (done) and send updated file + audit references.
- Marissa: attach network diagram + KMS flow chart used in the discussion.

Attachments: SIG_v2_answers.xlsx (updated, tracked changes), redwood-network-diagram.pdf

Best,
Marissa

--

Thanks for the clear notes and the tracked changes. FinBank confirms:
- Q6 wording accepted as-is (we'll rely on Redwood's tenant tagging for hosted).
- Q12 accepted with one procurement carve-out: for our hosted enterprise plan we require customer-managed KMS; please add a procurement note indicating this is a commercial-only option for hosted accounts.
